reviewer: Main session, independent of the bounded n105 prose author

checks.topic: Collective behavior, approximate neutrality and partial ionization
checks.reasoning: Electrical forces couple charged particles. Approximate charge balance on a sufficiently large scale does not require pointwise equality and does not imply the absence of electrons or ions. Neutral atoms can coexist with the charged species. The text explicitly includes collective response and does not classify every dilute ionized gas solely from equal charge counts.

checks.topic: Cathode space charge and positive column
checks.reasoning: A positive space-charge region fails the specific quasineutral-region condition. The modern statement is limited to that condition, not a universal denial of nonneutral plasmas or plasma sheaths. The nearly neutral positive column remains the source discharge-plasma example.

Excited discharge particles emit radiation. A fluorescent coating absorbs excitation radiation and re-emits visible light; choosing phosphors changes the visible spectrum. The passage does not confuse the tube discharge with the coating or imply that every discharge directly emits white light.

checks.topic: Gas-discharge laser application without power ranking
checks.reasoning: The passage discusses discharge-excited gas lasers, not every possible gas-laser pumping mechanism. Gain-medium identity alone cannot determine an absolute power ranking. Removing the unsupported superlative leaves the source application and distinctive directional radiation intact, without replacing it with an unverified record.

checks.topic: Metal electron-plasma model and positive ion cores
checks.reasoning: Accounting for conduction electrons leaves positive ion cores and maintains total charge balance. In the crystalline model, cores vibrate about lattice positions while electrons are mobile. The text explicitly treats electron plasma as a collective-response model, not a claim that a solid is an ionized gas, and does not exclude all diffusion processes.

The original density order and reciprocal-cubic-centimeter unit are retained. Number per volume has dimensions L^-3. At typical metallic electron densities the Fermi scale grows with density to the two-thirds power, so a classical dilute independent-particle description is not generally adequate. The quantum requirement is correctly scoped to an accurate description of the dense electrons, not to every possible classical approximation for lattice vibrations.

checks.topic: Stellar ionization and different interstellar phases
checks.reasoning: Heating and ionizing radiation produce ions and free electrons. A completely stripped atom leaves its positively charged nucleus. Density and temperature are independent physical quantities; dilute matter need not be cold. The modern paragraph explicitly limits its plasma claim to ionized interstellar components and retains warm as well as hot possibilities, rather than declaring all interstellar matter ionized.

For a Sun-like star, fusion of appropriate light nuclei into more tightly bound products releases energy. The text is explicitly scoped to such stars and explains an energy source replenishing outgoing radiation, without claiming that every fusion reaction or every phase of every star must release energy.

checks.topic: Controlled fusion versus a practical energy system
checks.reasoning: Reaction energy, sustained operation and useful net energy from a complete plant are distinct. Fuel-cycle reliability and material performance are separate constraints. The passage keeps the source research direction but makes no commercial deployment date, record-performance assertion or already-unlimited-energy claim.

references.title: Astronomy 2e, 20.2 Interstellar Gas
references.summary: The authored textbook describes ionized hydrogen regions and very hot interstellar gas separately from neutral and molecular phases. It also explains excitation radiation, phosphor absorption and visible emission in fluorescent lamps.

references.title: Fusion Energy Science, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
references.summary: PNNL identifies fuel-cycle and materials challenges in developing practical fusion systems, separately from sustaining a reaction. Its program includes tritium production, recovery, reuse and material behavior under interacting extreme conditions.

references.title: DOE Explains...Deuterium-Tritium Fusion Fuel
references.summary: DOE describes stellar fusion and the fuel-supply requirements of future fusion plants. It distinguishes potentially useful fuel resources from reliable production and supply-chain requirements.
